title: GitHub Actions policy file lint (.github/policy.rego): keep the line-1 regal ignore list current, including file-length, because all Actions policy lives in this one file
answers: bin/regal lint fails on .github/policy.rego after I added a new deny rule. What is wrong?
How do I suppress a regal lint rule for the Actions policy file?
Why are all the GitHub Actions Conftest rules kept in a single policy file?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego line 1 holds the comment `# regal ignore:directory-package-mismatch,file-length`, which tells regal lint to skip those two rules for the whole Actions policy file that holds every Conftest deny rule for .github/workflows and .github/actions.
Rule: The policy is kept in one file by design, so when a change grows it, add the needed regal rule name to the comma-separated list in that line-1 directive instead of splitting the file. The file-length suppression was added because the file sat only two lines under regal's limit, so any non-trivial addition triggered the lint failure.
Symptom: Adding a rule to the policy file made `bin/regal lint` report a file-length violation even though the Conftest checks themselves were fine.
Constraints: The directive only affects regal lint; it does not change what Conftest denies. Verify after editing by running `bin/regal lint` and `bin/conftest test` over .github/workflows and .github/actions.
Applies: Edits to .github/policy.rego that push the file past a regal limit; does not apply to workflow YAML files.
applies: Editing the GitHub Actions Conftest policy file .github/policy.rego and its regal lint directive.

search: Regal lint directive on line 1 of the GitHub Actions Conftest policy file: the comma-separated ignore list covers directory-package-mismatch and file-length, and is extended rather than splitting the file. Affects regal lint only, not what Conftest denies; does not apply to workflow YAML.
